answer: Yes. The story uses metaphor with subtlety and thematic purpose: “The past never stayed put. It moved toward whoever needed it” presents memory as something reshaped by emotional need. The mother’s habits become ways of keeping “the world arranged to her liking,” linking ordinary domestic actions to autonomy and resistance to decline. Her idiomatic “I’m not made of sugar” also gives her voice authenticity while making her later vulnerability to heat especially poignant.
